!
(pronounced as
Exclamation Mark
) is the second studio album by American rapper
Trippie Redd
, following his debut album
Life's a Trip
(2018). It was released on August 9, 2019, by TenThousand Projects and
Caroline Records
.
[
2
]
The album includes appearances from
The Game
,
Lil Duke
,
Lil Baby
and Redd's then-
girlfriend
Coi Leray
. The album also originally included the song "They Afraid of You" (featuring
Playboi Carti
), but it was removed from streaming services just six days after its release, on August 15, 2019.
[
3
]
Production was primarily handled by Hammad Beats, MTK,
OZ
, and
Chopsquad DJ
, among others.
!
sees Trippie Redd delve further into
emo rap
;
The Guardian
wrote that "[a]s part of the sonically esoteric but staggeringly high-selling emo-rap brigade, White knows how to blur the boundaries of hip-hop, to send shockwaves through its foundations."
[
4
]
The album was supported by two singles: "
Under Enemy Arms
" and "
Mac 10
" (featuring
Lil Baby
and Lil Duke). The record project was a commercial success, peaking at a higher point on the
Billboard 200
than
Life's a Trip
despite moving fewer
album-equivalent units
in its first week. The album was initially met with mixed critical reviews but resonated positively with listeners.
Background
On May 29, 2019, Trippie was featured on Beats 1 Radio and confirmed that his upcoming album would be called "!".
[
5
]
He also confirmed that
Playboi Carti
and
The Game
would be featured on the album.
[
5
]
The album's name is a reference to
XXXTentacion
's album
?
;
[
6
]
RapReviews opined that the album "is a tribute to his [Redd's] fallen comrade."
[
7
]
It has also been speculated that the name is short for the word 'Immortal'.
[
8
]
On May 29, 2019, Trippie Redd released the lead single from the project: a song called "Under Enemy Arms".
[
5
]
In June 2019, Redd stated that the purpose of the album was all about "elevation" and taking the next step in his career.
[
8
]
During the
2019 Wireless Festival
, Trippie confirmed the album's release date of 9 August 2019.
[
5
]
Promotion
Redd held an album release party in
Los Angeles
,
California
.
[
9
]
Songs
Tracks 1–7
The song "!" is the second collaboration between Trippie Redd (
left
) and producer Diplo (
right
).
The album's opener, "!", is produced by
Diplo
. The two previously collaborated on
Wish
.
[
10
]
The song opens with the voice of Apple's
Siri
repeating the album's title.
[
11
]
The next song, "Snake Skin", focuses on themes of
suicide
. Redd stated: "It's kind of suicidal, in a stay away from it type of shit… That's the whole concept of it, stay away from suicide. Don't worry about what other people say, you could be doing what they're doing or even better than them. It's just living life and knowing how to overcome shit."
[
10
]
The third track, "Be Yourself", stands as the sequel to "I Know How to Self Destruct" (
A Love Letter to You 2
).
[
12
]
Redd previewed the track in late 2018. Lyrically, the song calls for people to remain strong in the face of life's trials.
[
12
]
Redd also makes it clear that he will not tolerate anyone who fails to follow this principle.
[
12
]
The fourth song, "I Try", sees Redd detail a rocky relationship with his girlfriend.
[
13
]
The song became the center of controversy after
Kid Buu
claimed that Redd had stolen "I Try" from him on Instagram on September 21, 2019.
[
13
]
Buu cited a song on his computer titled "I TRY – 1.0," which was created on March 6, 2019. Later the same day, Buu released this version of the track, "I TRY / ++ LuV $ick".
[
13
]
Redd later stated that his own version of the song had existed since 2018. Redd also stated that Kid Buu had originally wanted to be on his song, but that he "kicked him off the song cause [
sic
] he was so damn trash".
[
13
]
The next track, "Immortal", sees Redd and featured artist
The Game
reflect on their use of drugs.
[
14
]
The track makes the first – and, to date, last – collaboration between the two artists.
[
14
]
In the sixth track, "Throw It Away", Redd recounts difficulties he has encountered with relationships.
[
15
]
The seventh track, "Keep Your Head Up", marks his second collaboration with producer
Murda Beatz
.
[
16
]
He previously collaborated with him on "Forever Ever" on his debut album,
Life's a Trip
.
[
16
]
On the song, Redd advocates for resilience and determination.
[
16
]
Tracks 8–13
The eighth track, "Riot" (stylized in all capitals), sees Redd tough talking.
[
17
]
He also mentions that he raps for his deceased brother.
[
17
]
The ninth song, "
Mac 10
", serves as the album's second single.
[
18
]
The song is produced by
Wheezy
and
Bobby Raps
and is a collaboration between Trippie Redd,
Lil Duke
and
Lil Baby
.
[
18
]
Its title refers to the
MAC-10
,
[
18
]
a compact,
blowback operated
machine pistol
/
submachine gun
which was developed by
Gordon Ingram
in 1964.
[
19
]
Redd debuted the song at a concert in March 2019, performing it with Lil Duke.
[
20
]
In an interview with
Zane Lowe
, Redd stated: "Baby was sleep [
sic
] on the couch and Duke was up with me, we were just smoking and vibing then Wheezy came in the studio, I asked him for a beat. I did the chorus, Duke got on it then I woke Baby's ass up told him [
sic
] to record his shit… He took damn near 30 minutes but he woke up out his sleep and got that out the way."
[
21
]
Lil Duke and Lil Baby have previously collaborated on "Up" (
Perfect Timing
), "I'm Gettin' Paid," and "Still On My Shit".
[
18
]
"Mac 10" marks Redd's first collaboration with either artist.
[
18
]
The tenth track, "Everything BoZ", features Redd's then-girlfriend
Coi Leray
.
[
22
]
The title of the track is a play off Leray's debut project
Everythingcoz
.
[
22
]
One of Redd's lines in the song's chorus, 'P*ssy n*gga know I came from toting poles', likely refers to his early hit "
Poles 1469
".
[
22
]
The following song, "Under Enemy Arms", is
!
'
s lead single.
[
23
]
The song juxtaposes violent lyrics over an upbeat, orchestral instrumental.
[
23
]
On May 31, 2019, Trippie Redd published the music video for "Under Enemy Arms".
[
24
]
The end of the video sees the appearance of a rainbow-colored rat, seemingly referring to
6ix9ine
testifying as a witness for the state against his criminal associates
.
[
23
]
[
24
]
The twelfth song, "Lil Wayne" was written by
the rapper of the same name
as well as Redd. However, review site
Pitchfork
fictitiously claimed that the song "isn't indebted to him, stylistically or otherwise."
[
25
]
Initially, the record project was supposed to contain a collaboration with Lil Wayne, but after the song leaked online Redd replaced it with "Lil Wayne".
[
8
]
The thirteenth and final song on the album is called "Signing Off".
Other
The album previously contained the track "They Afraid of You" (featuring
Playboi Carti
), but it was later removed from streaming services and physical releases just six days after its release, on August 15, 2019.
[
26
]
RapReviews
speculated that there had been sample clearance issues.
[
7
]

]
!
was met with mixed reviews. At
Metacritic
, which assigns a
normalized
rating out of 100 to reviews from professional publications, the album received an
average
score of 59, which indicates "mixed or average reviews", based on 6 reviews.
[
29
]
The Guardian
described the album as "compelling but contradictory emo-rap", noting lyrical contradictions and concluding it "is doubtless part of the genre's forward march – but it's hard to get past the sense that White has sacrificed a coherent artistic identity in the name of progress."
[
4
]
Pitchfork
opined that the "songs touch on being true to oneself at all costs, but these half-baked lessons land flat since Redd himself doesn't really have an identity, musical or otherwise", and concluded that "the most enjoyable moments feel like controlled chaos. Redd […] does at least sound more composed. That's to his credit as a person but it's not to his advantage as an artist."
[
25
]
Nevertheless, community feedback suggested that "!" has resonated positively with many listeners, many of whom described the album as "underrated" or "overhated".
[
30
]
"
Mac 10
" and "Immortal", among other songs, were identified as highlights of the album.
[
25
]
Blurred Culture
said that "
!
is truly a personal glimpse into his [Redd's] own life."
[
9
]
The magazine concluded: "The album has a bit of everything for everyone. … On this album, Trippie Redd does a great job of trying new sounds and styles. It's still dark, emotional Trippie, but he is really showcasing his versatility here."
[
9
]
Commercial performance
The album debuted at number three on the US
Billboard
200
with 51,000
album-equivalent units
, of which 7,000 were pure album sales in its first week.
[
31
]
The album charted behind only
Slipknot
's
We Are Not Your Kind
and
Rick Ross
'
Port of Miami 2
.
[
32
]
!
thus became Redd's third top 10 album in the
United States
, all three of which charted in the previous 12 months.
[
32
]
From the record project, "
Under Enemy Arms
" peaked at No. 94 on the
Billboard
Hot 100
, giving Redd his tenth appearance on that chart.
[
32
]
Mac 10
(64) and "Snake Skin" (87) also charted on the
Billboard
Hot 100. "!" (12) and "They Afraid of You" (21) charted within the Bubbling Under Hot 100. On 8 October 2020, "Under Enemy Arms" achieved Gold certification from the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA).
[
33
]
On 9 November 2022, "Mac 10" achieved Platinum certification from the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA).
